sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with Anglo-American commercial-law overlays in the corporate and fiduciary sectors

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de julio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley 61 de 2015; Articles 1 to 40; supplementary application of the Panamanian Civil and Commercial Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Archivo Central, Panama City, Republic of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Public Deed of Constitution of a Private Interest Foundation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under Law 25 of 1995, there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Foundation Charter must state a definitive initial endowment (patrimonio fundacional) sufficient for the declared purpose. Any undelivered endowment must be identified and, if cash, held in a designated bank account of the Foundation pending registration; no general statutory escrow account is required for private interest foundations, but customs bonded-warehouse approval will require a surety bond or customs guarantee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLUTION: By unanimous written consent of the Foundation Council of [NAME], it is resolved: (1) the initial endowment subscribed by the Founder is accepted, credited to the Foundation's patrimony, and capitalized; (2) the registered office in Panama City, Republic of Panama, is adopted, and the designated Resident Agent is confirmed; (3) the first Council members and officers are appointed, and the Chairperson and Secretary are empowered to execute banking, registry and administrative instruments; (4) the Foundation seal, ledgers and accounting books are approved; (5) the Resident Agent is directed to obtain Public Registry inscription, RUC registration, and all licenses required for the bonded wine and spirits wholesale activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Panama City Notary Public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish with the required clauses: name, registered domicile, purpose, initial endowment, Foundation Council, beneficiaries, reserved powers, and disposition of assets. The Founder must execute the public deed before a Panamanian notary; the Resident Agent must accept the appointment in the same instrument or by separate notarized letter.
required_dossiers: Founder's passport or corporate powers if the Founder is a legal entity
Declaration or certificate of initial endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If defects are detected before registration, the deed may be amended by a new notarial instrument or the Foundation Charter may be revoked; if the Public Registry later queries a clause, the Founder executes a notarial addendum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the original public deed and one notarized copy to the Public Registry. Complete the registration request and pay the official filing fee. The Registry will issue a certified certificate of inscription and juridical existence.
required_dossiers: Original Escritura Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado
Founder identification or good-standing certificate if corporate founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A registry observation (nota de reparo) may be cured by filing the requested correction or a supplementary public deed, or by seeking reconsideration before the Registrar General within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal appointment of Foundation Council members and officers; adoption of governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council and Resident Agent, recorded in the Foundation protocol ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first written Council meeting; accept the appointments of Chairperson, Secretary, and Treasurer; adopt the minutes; issue a power of attorney to the Resident Agent; and open the Foundation protocol and accounting books. Where the Charter already names the Council members, formal acceptance is recorded and filed with the Resident Agent.
required_dossiers: List of Foundation Council members and officers
Resident Agent appointment or power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointment is questioned by authorities or third parties, call an extraordinary Council session and record a corrective resolution, or execute an amendment to the Foundation Charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification (RUC) and municipal operational registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipality of Panama for Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RUC registration application to DGI using the registered Foundation Charter. Obtain the Foundation's tax identification number and, if operations are commercial, apply for a municipal Aviso de Operación in the district where the warehouse is located. Notify DGI of any required withholding and advance tax estimates.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of registered Foundation Charter
Resident Agent certificate and RUC application form
Tax registration forms for legal entities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficient applications are returned online or at the counter; correct the observations and resubmit. For DGI determinations, an administrative reconsideration or appeal to the Administrative Tax Court may be filed within the applicable deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, commercial, customs, sanitary, and fire licensing for bonded wine and spirits warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI); Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA); Ministerio de Salud (MINSA); Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the commercial operation permit application with MICI and the municipal authority; apply to ANA for authorization as a customs bonded warehouse for alcoholic beverages; obtain the MINSA sanitary permit; obtain the Fire Department inspection and structural clearance; and register workers with CSS and MITRADEL for occupational safety and insurance.
required_dossiers: Registered Foundation Charter and Foundation Council appointment
Lease or title of the warehouse
Facility plans and structural load certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For technical inspection deficiencies, submit correction reports and pay any re-inspection fees; for denied licenses, exhaust the administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) available under each agency's procedures within the applicable time limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección Nacional de Comercio; Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) - Depósito Aduanero; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Licencia Comercial Industrial (MICI-Municipal); Customs Bonded Warehouse Authorization (ANA); Sanitary Permit for Alcoholic Beverage Storage and Handling (MINSA)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Registro Ambiental) under Law 41 of 1998 and its implementing regulations; a full Environmental Impact Study is not required for sealed bonded storage of wine and spirits unless storage capacity, expansion, or associated infrastructure triggers a higher environmental classification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant industrial process effluents are expected; any sanitary or cleaning wastewater must meet Panamanian discharge standards: pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 110 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L. For sealed bonded storage there is no point-source VOC emission, but ethanol vapor monitoring and ventilation controls apply if bulk storage, decanting, or spill handling is undertaken. Damaged wines and spirits, empty barrels, and packaging waste must be managed as industrial solid waste under MiAMBIENTE and MINSA requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural load inspection of the warehouse by a licensed engineer and municipal works approval; occupational health and safety registration with MITRADEL; worker's risk insurance with CSS; civil-defense and building-code clearance for warehouse occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), República de Panamá; official electronic portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (SICD e-services) and https://www.mef.gob.pa; customs counterpart: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), https://www.ana.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute a notarized power of attorney appointing a Panamanian resident legal representative / registered agent. Step 2: Register the Private Interest Foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva) with the Registro Público and obtain the certificate of registration. Step 3: File DGI online registration via SICD / Sede Electrónica to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC), stating the foundation's corporate purpose (wholesale bonded trade of wines and spirits, ISIC 4632), fiscal domicile, and statutory agent. Step 4: Obtain the DGI resolution assigning the RUC together with ITBMS registration and, where applicable, the ANA bonded-warehouse operator cross-reference. Step 5: Activate the electronic-invoicing profile (emisor fiscal electrónico) through an authorized certification provider. Statutory completion target: 10–15 business days from full submission.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies a civil-law classification: no US-style check-the-box election exists. A Private Interest Foundation is a separate juridical person under Law 25 of 1995 and may elect the annual flat tax of PAB 300 (Article 24, Law 25/1995) rather than entity-level income taxation, provided it performs no Panamanian-source commercial activities. Where bonded trading is conducted in Panama, the territorial corporate income tax applies only to Panamanian-source revenue; the foundation may elect the SISA simplified regime if gross receipts are at or below the statutory threshold (currently PAB 200,000), and affiliated resident entities may elect fiscal-group consolidation. No hybrid-mismatch election is recognized; Panama applies internal source rules, transfer-pricing rules, and anti-deferral provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS), a destination-principle VAT; supplemented for this scope by the Impuesto Selectivo al Consumo (ISC) on alcoholic beverages.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ITBMS registration is mandatory from the first habitual taxable supply in Panama; no general de minimis turnover threshold applies. Exporters and bonded-warehouse operators must hold full ITBMS registration to issue zero-rated export invoices and claim input credits/refunds. Small taxpayers with Panamanian-source gross receipts at or below PAB 200,000 may elect the SISA simplified regime, which consolidates income tax and ITBMS; bonded wine/spirit operators remain required to maintain full registration and electronic-invoice compliance in all cases.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory fiscal e-invoicing is enforced through the DGI's SICD platform. All invoices must be issued through an authorized certification service provider, electronically signed, and covered by a DGI digital stamp ('sellado digital') carrying a QR verification code before delivery to the purchaser. Export invoices must quote the ANA export declaration (DUA) number and be transmitted under the DGI technical protocol in near-real time; bonded-warehouse removals require an electronic dispatch notice linked to the ANA single window. Incomplete or late transmission is sanctioned as non-issuance of the invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports—including removals of duty-suspended aged Scotch and Bordeaux wines from an ANA bonded warehouse to a foreign destination—are zero-rated (tax at 0% with input credit/refund entitlement) provided: (i) the PIF is a DGI- and ANA-registered exporter; (ii) goods physically depart Panama under a validated DUA and transport document; (iii) the purchaser is a non-resident and the sale is documented as offshore; (iv) the invoice is an electronically stamped export invoice; (v) settlement is in USD or a freely convertible currency with bank documentation. Panama imposes no statutory FX repatriation term because the US dollar is legal tender; the 180-day window is applied as the banking and audit benchmark for documenting export proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduana – DUA) validated by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) with physical exit confirmation
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing shipment from Panama to the foreign destination
DGI-stamped electronic commercial invoice bearing the export legend and DUA cross-reference
Packing list and lot/weight schedule identifying each wine and spirit lot, bottle sizes, and precise alcohol strength
Certificate of origin or supplier's origin statement (e.g., EUR.1 / Annex declaration) where preferential duty treatment is sought
Inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice evidencing USD settlement of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Misdeclared export zero-rating triggers re-characterization of the removal as a domestic taxable supply: ITBMS at 7% (plus applicable ISC on alcoholic beverages) together with monthly interest, surcharges of 25%–100% of the omitted tax, and fines under the Código Fiscal and DGI sanction schedules; retroactive clawback assessments are permitted within the five-year statutory term, extended where concealment or forgery is found. Criminal defraudación fiscal liability, including custodial exposure, may attach to directors, the protector, and the resident agent for simulated exports or forged DUA/B/L documentation, and the ANA may suspend or cancel the bonded-warehouse license and delist the operator from the exporter registry. Panama's absence of exchange controls means 'repatriation' compliance is assessed on documentary consistency, bank credit advisements, and AML indicators rather than a statutory day count.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent. Panama has no conventional central bank; the regime is anchored on full dollarization with the U.S. dollar as unrestricted legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction with no exchange controls on either current-account or capital-account transactions. The balboa circulates only as coins pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar. Profit remittances and capital transfers are freely permitted without FX authorization. However, the territorial corporate income tax (25%) and withholding rules on dividends distributed to non-resident individuals (potential 10% surcharge) require the foundation to document exempt foreign-source income separately from Panamanian-source income; no FX licensing or conversion approval is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline on export receipts. Proceeds from bonded wine and spirit exports may be retained and disbursed freely in USD. Nevertheless, exporters must comply with tax filing obligations, SBP AML/CFT reporting under Law 23/2015 for transactions above USD 10,000, and customs exit documentation through the SIEC system including bonded-warehouse withdrawal documents ('Libranza' or 'Solicitud de Salida') and destination declarations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Offshore digital EMIs are not licensed by the SBP and cannot serve as the primary treasury, escrow, or settlement account for a Panamanian PIF. Reliance on unsupervised EMIs creates unlicensed money-services exposure under Law 23/2015 and will typically cause SBP-regulated banks to reject incoming transfers as an AML red flag. A non-local EMI may be acceptable only for low-value ancillary disbursements if it is duly licensed in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction, is linked to verified trade documentation, and is never used for capital contributions or bonded-trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Credit and account-opening interviews are normally required in person for the founder, foundation council members, and ultimate beneficial owners. A fully remote onboarding is available at select tier-1 banks only under enhanced due diligence, subject to video identification, apostilled corporate registry documents, and successful screening against SBP and OFAC watchlists. Because a PIF has no shareholders, the bank will additionally require the notarized foundation charter, the current council resolution appointing officers, and a full look-through of the founder, protector, and beneficiaries. Physical presence remains the default expectation for a Medium-Risk Enhanced bonded-trade client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undocumented PIF UBO structure involving a silent founder, undisclosed beneficiary, or bearer-like foundation council
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Foundation Charter ('Acta de Fundación'); current 'Resolución del Consejo de la Fundación' appointing the council and officers; sworn founder declaration identifying the source of the initial endowment; complete identification documents of each beneficiary and council member; and a written UBO look-through memorandum certified by foundation counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of wealth for a high-value capital injection, such as liquidation of foreign assets, private credit, or inheritance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical bank statements, audited financial statements, executed sale-and-purchase contracts, notarial inheritance documents, an independent wealth-origin memorandum, and a signed statement of the contributing entity and beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade mispricing or dual-invoicing suspicion on bonded Scotch and Bordeaux wine purchases, which are high-duty commodities prone to invoice manipulation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chamber-of-commerce-certified commercial invoices, authenticated purchase contracts with matched payment milestones, marine and airway bills, bonded-warehouse storage warrants, insurance certificates, customs bond entries, and SIEC import/export declarations reconciled by quantity, vintage, cask number, and bottle count.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, OFAC, or PEP exposure arising from foreign distribution or use of USD correspondent clearing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated denied-party screening results for every counterparty and beneficial owner; end-user and end-use certificates for each shipment; geoproofed removal and delivery receipts from bonded warehouses; and an updated KYC file screened against OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions lists at onboarding and on every threshold-crossing transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Transfer the initial endowment through a segregated Capital Escrow Account at a top-tier SBP-regulated bank. The contributing entity must send a SWIFT MT103 wire in USD with full originator and beneficial-owner data (no name shielding), narrative 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF under Panama Law 25 of 1995 and Foundation Charter', and the foundation's registry reference. The receiving bank's compliance team must pre-approve the wire, and a source-of-funds brief and Know-Your-Originator certificate must be submitted before the first transfer. The bank will classify the proceeds as capital and will not commingle them with trade operations; subsequent release toward bonded-trade purchases must be supported by a notarized foundation council resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for operational and trade disbursements to suppliers, bonded-warehouse operators, and customs brokers, with high-value USD settlement executed via New York correspondent clearing (Fedwire/CHIPS). For bulk aged Scotch and Bordeaux purchases, use Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 with documents comprising a full set of bills of lading, certificate of origin, bonded-warehouse transfer slips, and insurance certificate. Same-day local disbursements to customs and logistics counterparties may use the local ACH Panama and clearing-house rails, but time-critical treasury payments should be executed as USD wires over the correspondent network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable forwards and FX options with SBP-licensed counterparties (hedging Bordeaux purchase inventory)
GBP/USD deliverable forwards and FX options (hedging aged Scotch acquisition costs)
Cross-currency swaps (EUR-USD and GBP-USD) on inventory financing facilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in regional Latin American currencies, including COP, PEN, and MXN, for secondary-market distribution proceeds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Panama Private Interest Foundation Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual / Annual Foundation Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March of each calendar year for the prevailing annual tax liability; payable annually for as long as the foundation remains registered in the Public Registry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment interest of 1%; administrative fine of up to 100% of the unpaid tax; chronic non-payment may result in Public Registry annotation of the foundation as an irregular entity, RUC cancellation, and enforced strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax / Non-Taxpayer Sworn Declaration (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta y/o No Causante)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard calendar-year foundation, on or before 31 March of the following tax year; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines per Panama Tax Code; monthly interest on any Panama-source tax due; penalties of up to 100% of the omitted tax; prolonged failure to file may suspend the foundation’s taxpayer identification (RUC) and limit legal transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Commercial Operation License Annual Renewal (Aviso de Operación / Patente Municipal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal Treasury of the district of the registered office or bonded premises (e.g., Municipio de Panamá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each year for continuing activities; initial filing required before commencement of bonded trade or wholesale operations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 10% of the license fee up to a 100% cap; non-renewed license permits municipal closure of premises and administrative fines for operating without a current Aviso de Operación.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Bonded Warehouse Annual Authorization Continuation (Renovación Anual de Depósito Fiscal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA), Regimes Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of the bonded warehouse authorization; the operator must submit the yearly stock report, compliance certificate, security update, and current customs bond.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew cancels the bonded warehouse regime; goods held in bond must be re-exported, transferred, or entered for customs within the authorized term; ANA administrative fines apply for unauthorized storage of excisable wines and spirits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Sworn Update (Confirmación Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each year reflecting data as at 31 December; changes in ultimate beneficial owner or foundation beneficiary appointment must be updated within 15 working days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines imposed by DGI for late or inaccurate UBO confirmation; serious or repeated non-compliance may suspend the foundation’s RUC and restrict registration of transfers and notarial acts in Panama.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory mandatory independent audit applies to a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. A certified audit is mandatory only if required by the foundation charter or a founder resolution, if the foundation engages in Panama-source commercial activity and DGI or ANA requires CPA-attested financial statements in connection with a bonded warehouse or excise license, or if ordered by a competent court.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama has adopted IFRS for general financial reporting purposes. An inactive Private Interest Foundation may maintain simple cash-basis records; a foundation operating bonded wine and spirits wholesale activity must maintain IFRS-compliant books and records, including stock inventories, customs documents, and physical movement registers, expressed in Spanish and US Dollar or its functional currency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Private Interest Foundation has no share capital and therefore no share-transfer reconciliation. The registered agent must maintain permanent identification of the founder, foundation council members, protector if any, and beneficiaries expressed in the foundation deed. Charter amendments affecting these persons must be registered in the Public Registry. In addition, an annual beneficial-ownership sworn update must be confirmed with DGI each calendar year; any economic interest or beneficiary substitution occurring during the year must be reported to the registered agent and DGI within 15 working days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (flat rate on net taxable income from Panamanian-source activities, Article 699 of the Código Fiscal; a compliant Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995 is exempt from corporate income tax on foreign-source bonded trade income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate for a compliant PIF whose bonded wine/spirits trade occurs exclusively outside Panama (territorial taxation); 25% on Panamanian-source net income if the PIF engages in local commercial activity; dividend distributions by a PIF to beneficiaries are exempt from Panamanian dividend tax; no other statutory tax holidays apply to ISIC 4632 bonded trade

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 120 (Declaración Anual de Rentas - Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the SISTEMA T@S portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI; https://tas.dgi.gob.pa)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; statutory advance payments (Anticipos) are due in March, June, September and December each year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the filing deadline is 31 March

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registro Único de Contribuyentes tax registration ID of the PIF
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the 15-digit RUC certificate; a local registered agent must obtain the RUC before filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year covered by the return (from 1 January to 31 December or other permitted fiscal year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact fiscal year-end; a foreign-controlled PIF may adopt a non-calendar fiscal year with prior DGI approval

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income exempt or not subject to Panamanian tax (foreign-source bonded trade proceeds)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full gross proceeds of bonded warehouse sales physically delivered in UK/France and all offshore revenue; attach a sworn affidavit and supporting bills of lading, warehouse warrants and sales contracts

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income deriving from Panamanian-source commercial activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero if no Panamanian-source sales occurred; any sale with delivery, consumption or transfer of title inside Panama must be reported here

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary expenses attributable to the production of taxable Panamanian-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may claim costs directly tied to Panamanian-source revenue only; foreign storage and freight costs attributable to exempt foreign revenue are not deductible against the exempt income and should be reported in the reconciliation memo

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable gross revenue less allowable deductions (base for the 25% ISR)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a fully foreign-source PIF operation, enter zero; if a portion is Panamanian-source, compute that portion only

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax on Box 47 at the statutory rate (25%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the tax due; if Box 47 is zero, enter zero and rely on the territorial exemption declaration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments and any withholding credits applicable to the PIF
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach copies of the four Anticipo deposit vouchers; the minimum quarterly advance for a bonded trade entity with negligible Panamanian-source income may be zero if no prior-year tax liability existed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable after credits, or the credit balance to be offset/carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the net balance; any payment must be made via the T@S portal in USD (Balboa) on or before 31 March, and a tax clearance certificate (Paz y Salvo) is issued only after payment is settled

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due (minimum B/.50; maximum B/.2,500); late payment surcharge of 15% of the tax due; default interest accrues at 1.5% per month; non-declaration of an exempt PIF may trigger a B/.200 to B/.500 penalty plus loss of the Paz y Salvo, which blocks customs, banking and bonded-warehouse operations

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax (Article 733-A of the Código Fiscal) applies to distributions from Panamanian-source profits of corporations; distributions made by a Private Interest Foundation to its beneficiaries are legally characterized as foundation distributions (not dividends) and are exempt from the 10% WHT under Law 25 of 1995, subject to proof that the distributed funds originated from foreign-source or otherwise exempt income
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama does not maintain a comprehensive income tax treaty with the United Kingdom or France as of 2025; relief therefore operates unilaterally: the PIF must evidence foreign source through (i) a certificate of the foreign bonded warehouse (UK HMRC excise-warehouse warrant or French Douane document), (ii) sales contracts confirmed outside Panama, and (iii) a Declaración Jurada attached to Form 120; where a counterparty asks for treaty residence status, the DGI issues a Certificado de Residencia Fiscal (TRC) based on physical presence, registered address and tax-filing history; the TRC application is made through T@S with the registered agent's notarized power of attorney and a B/.50 fee
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident lenders is subject to 6% statutory WHT if the underlying debt is attributable to Panamanian-source investment, but interest on foreign financing employed abroad for the acquisition of Scotch/Bordeaux inventory held outside Panama is foreign-source and exempt; IP royalties paid for the use of trademarks or processes within Panama are subject to 25% WHT, while royalties for foreign vintner/brand use abroad remain outside Panamanian tax jurisdiction; no WHT is levied on PIF beneficiary distributions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File arise where associated transactions in a fiscal year exceed B/.2,000,000 (USD 2,000,000) or where gross revenue exceeds B/.2,000,000; a Country-by-Country report is required for a PIF that is part of a multinational group with consolidated revenue of at least B/.750,000,000; an Informative Return of transactions with related parties (Form ICT) is required when cross-border related-party transactions exceed B/.250,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: A Private Interest Foundation is under an economic-substance presumption under Law 25 of 1995, Law 23 of 2015 and OECD BEPS Pillar Two: the PIF must maintain a Panamanian registered agent, an internal register of council members and beneficiaries (escriturada), meeting minutes, and real external contracts with the UK/French bonded warehouses; if DGI determines the PIF carries on economic activity wholly or partly within Panama, the territorial exemption lapses and 25% ISR plus 10% annual interest is levied on the recapture base; no separate ESR notification is filed in Panama, but the DGI, the Superintendencia de Bancos and the beneficial-ownership registry may request substance evidence in any AML/CTF review

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file Form 120, materially understating Panamanian-source income, or falsely characterizing physically delivered wine/spirits inside Panama (including Colon Free Zone resale to domestic consumers) as foreign-source bonded trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment of the evaded tax plus default interest at 1.5% monthly; administrative fine of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax; criminal penalty of 2 to 5 years imprisonment; placement on the DGI public defaulter register; disqualification from customs bonded operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and fines; the corporate veil is pierced, allowing seizure of personal assets; courts may issue travel bans (impedimentos de salida) and extradition requests under mutual legal assistance treaties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a pure shell — no council meetings, no economic decision-making in Panama, no registered-agent activity, no written contracts with the UK/French bonded warehouses — used solely to avoid EU excise duties, estate taxes or anti-money-laundering scrutiny
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive loss of the Law 25 tax exemption; 25% ISR recapture of all prior exempt income with 10% annual interest; fines of B/.10,000 to B/.100,000 under Law 23 of 2015; risk of being listed as a non-cooperative entity by foreign tax authorities and being excluded from correspondent banking lines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution to creditors and beneficiaries; directors criminally prosecuted for fraudulent insolvency or fraud (Código Penal Articles 265 and 266) with 3 to 8 years imprisonment; disqualification from serving as company officers in Panama for 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or falsifying the mandatory beneficial ownership (UBO) return with the Registro Público under Law 23 of 2015 and Resolution 146 of 2020, or routing bonded-trade proceeds through OFAC-sanctioned or high-risk counterparties without enhanced due diligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines per violation of B/.10,000 to B/.1,000,000 against the foundation and its registered agent; suspension or cancellation of the registered agent license; freezing of the PIF's bank accounts; potential international financial blacklisting of the entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Council members personally liable for AML fines; imprisonment up to 3 years for money laundering where proceeds are knowingly derived from illicit distilled-spirits trafficking; travel bans and international arrest warrants may be issued

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Panamanian bonded/free-zone license to release Scotch whisky or Bordeaux wine into the domestic Panamanian market without payment of the alcohol tax (Impuesto de Alcohol), the unitary spirits surcharge and the 7% ITBMS, or without proper customs despacho from the receiving bond
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate seizure of the bonded stock; fine equal to 1 to 3 times the evaded excise duty; suspension or cancellation of the customs bonded-warehouse operating permit; publication in the customs sanctions registry; reference to the DGI for criminal tax evasion proceedings if ITBMS is also evaded
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several responsibility of the licensee directors for the full unpaid excise and ITBMS amount; closure of the bond with consequential civil damages to the storage owners; directors face imprisonment of 1 to 4 years for customs smuggling (Ley de Delitos Aduaneros)
